review_scope: One combined correctness, clean-code and boundary-safety review of the new real-roster withdrawal diagnostic and focused tests. Prior production roster, FP, lifecycle, C dialogue and scan reviews are reused at their own identities.

decision.clearance_scope: One healthy control first, then withdrawn_backing with the exact separately bound 505 Lua literal on compiled 5182 hosted native and fresh verified roots. No binary/source relabelling. A failed healthy control must not unlock the withdrawal run.

source_assessment: The mode calls the actual reference provider REMOVE operation once, only after a validated real FIRST answer has returned with a nonempty served key. The initial provider call and borrow have ended before the REMOVE call; no reentrant Engine entry is added.

REMOVE changes the real authoritative roster record. It deliberately bypasses campaign-event bookkeeping, leaves Core backing lists, entity/key resolution and pose records unchanged, and returns the original FIRST answer unchanged. No fabricated refused answer, synthetic callback exception, Core mutation or query-time record seeding is used.

Only a successful removed acknowledgement increments withdrawal credit. The next observed scan operation must be ENTRY. Success requires the primary entity_scan.refused marker together with roster.key and has ended, exactly zero request faults, exactly one reply fault, and the captured first fault scan reply: result refused. An acknowledgement failure or unrelated fatal cannot satisfy the mode.
The failure verdict uses captured Lua counters and failure text. The new code adds no Engine/provider reads after Fatal or Poisoned; it does not claim postfatal buffer or engine-state inspection.

The additional counters distinguish the deliberate real-provider removal from actual campaign lifecycle events. No raw entity index or pointer is introduced, and no new physical solver, fallback, floating arithmetic or production decision is added.
